profile.address: Electron Avenue, Salem Township, Luzerne County, PA 18601
profile.reading: Nautilus Cryptomine, this registry's Building 1 of two mapped structures at the site, sits on Electron Avenue, Salem Township, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania 18601, co-located at Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear power plant. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage and a Talen Energy SEC filing exhibit on Nautilus Cryptomine LLC, the facility is a joint venture between cryptomining and data center company TeraWulf and Cumulus Coin, drawing power directly from the co-located nuclear plant, a behind the meter power arrangement that has drawn broader industry and regulatory attention as large compute and cryptomining loads increasingly seek direct connections to nuclear generation for reliable, carbon free power. The site's total IT capacity is reported at 50 megawatts. TeraWulf is a publicly traded Bitcoin mining and, increasingly, AI and high performance computing infrastructure company that has positioned nuclear adjacent sites like this one as a differentiator for both low cost, reliable power and a lower carbon profile relative to fossil fuel powered mining operations. This registry's own OpenStreetMap sourced mapping shows two separate buildings at this site, numbered west to east; this row represents the westernmost, Building 1, while a companion row, Building 2, tracks the second structure. No square footage or facility specific certification detail was located for this specific building this session. The Nautilus Cryptomine campus draws its power directly from the 2.5GW Susquehanna nuclear power station, one of the largest nuclear plants in the United States, through a joint venture TeraWulf formed with plant owner Talen Energy in 2021. The arrangement was reported as the first data center facility in the country to source its power directly from a nuclear plant behind the meter rather than through the regional grid. Talen later purchased TeraWulfs minority stake in the joint venture in 2024, giving the power company full ownership of the physical campus while TeraWulf has continued to describe its operations there as unaffected by the ownership change.

reading.body:
Nautilus Cryptomine is a 50 MW campus in Salem Township, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania, co-located at Talen Energy's Susquehanna nuclear plant. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 50 MW of IT load is roughly 1,250 racks. The campus consists of two buildings and draws power from a nuclear source.

Pennsylvania has published specifications for four data center facilities totaling 22.2 MW of IT capacity. Nautilus ranks fifth among mapped facilities in the state by published megawatts, though most of the 14 mapped facilities in Pennsylvania publish no capacity figure. This campus alone represents 225% of the state's other three published capacities combined.

The facility is registered as a joint venture between TeraWulf and Cumulus Coin. No certifications are published for this campus. The research status is marked exhausted, meaning additional operator specifications are not expected to be found.
